title: Founding Fundsmith with the buy-good-companies-do-nothing doctrine
statement: After selling Tullett Prebon, Smith founded Fundsmith with a stated strategy of buying a small number of high-quality, cash-generative consumer and healthcare franchises and holding them indefinitely — 'buy good companies, don't overpay, do nothing.'
outcome: The fund became the largest actively managed equity fund in the UK within a decade and Smith the country's highest-profile fund manager, with assets exceeding £20 billion.

title: Buy-and-hold portfolio turnover near zero
statement: Fundsmith's approach holds roughly 25-30 stocks and trades almost never — annual turnover around 5% — on the argument that trading is a cost with no expected return.
outcome: The tax efficiency and compounding of the low-turnover approach became the fund's structural edge; Smith presented each year's full holdings and trades transparently.

title: The annual 'show me the money' shareholder meetings
statement: Smith instituted free public annual meetings at which he presents complete performance, holdings and reasoning, in plain language and often scathing commentary on industry practice.
outcome: The meetings, at which he has famously told investors who don't understand the strategy to leave, set a transparency benchmark and drew thousands in person and online.

title: Concentrated bets on consumer franchises
statement: From inception, the fund has concentrated in companies like Nestlé, Microsoft, Novo Nordisk, Stryker and PepsiCo — asset-light, high-return, cash-generative businesses with durable competitive positions.
outcome: The concentration, up to roughly 8% per name, produced top-decile performance for the first decade, though periods of underperformance after 2020 tested the discipline.

title: Tullett Prebon — building and selling the interdealer broker
statement: Smith joined and later led Collins Stewart and then Tullett Prebon, building an interdealer broking business and eventually selling the firm to TP ICAP in 2016.
outcome: The sale provided the capital for his philanthropy and Fundsmith stake; Smith donated £25 million of the proceeds to fund a cancer centre in Kent.

title: Smithson Investment Trust — the quality-factor listed vehicle
statement: Smith launched a listed investment trust applying the Fundsmith discipline to smaller and mid-cap global quality stocks, raising £822 million in the largest UK trust IPO in years.
outcome: The vehicle performed well in its early years; Smith later announced its planned wind-up in 2024 when it traded persistently at a discount, returning capital rather than managing a structurally discounted fund — consistent with his stated contempt for asset-gathering.
